summary:
APULA is a Next.js App Router, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS dashboard built to evaluate spacecraft flammability, microgravity and partial-gravity combustion physics, and empirical NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) flight test evidence in one interface. Instead of running brute-force supercomputer simulations or relying on a black-box neural network, APULA uses Super Intelligence to compress computationally intensive 3D Navier-Stokes and radiative fluid dynamics into O(1) lookup tables and reduced-order Biot-Damköhler equations, enabling sub-millisecond execution and interactive visualization at 60 FPS.

Integrating 654 experimental records across 8 NASA PSI campaigns with physics-based combustion modeling, APULA makes spacecraft fire research easier to retrieve, compare, and interpret. Its interactive 3D wind tunnel and adjustable environmental parameters reveal how gravity and atmospheric conditions influence flame behavior. Flammability maps visualize combustion boundaries and transitions. A Dynamic PSI Investigation Ranker organizes research across prevention, detection, and suppression, complemented by empirical matching and cross-investigation comparisons.

By distinguishing actual NASA measurements from simulated results and projected lunar-flight scenarios through provenance labels, APULA helps users identify gaps in current knowledge and explore fire-safety challenges for future human space exploration.
details:
APULA: Atmospheric Prediction & Unified Low-gravity Analysis

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Flame in Freefall

ᜀᜉᜓᜎ /ʔɐ.pʊˈla/ [noun] the Filipino word to put out / extinguish a fire.

Summary

NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database holds decades of low-gravity combustion results, but the brief is right that the data is hard to find, harder to compare, and harder to interpret. APULA is a web dashboard that does three things with this:

  1. Ranks the 13 combustion investigations by how relevant they are to a fire-safety scenario you choose (ISS, Lunar base, Mars habitat, EVA suit), and explains each score.
  2. Interprets the scenario with a transparent, reduced-order physics model that predicts whether a flame ignites, what regime it burns in, how fast it spreads, and how that shifts with gravity, pressure, oxygen, airflow and electric field.
  3. Grounds every prediction by showing the closest real flight runs from the bundled PSI data, so a user can see where the model is backed by evidence and where it is extrapolating.

This approach directly reflects a gap identified in the brief: PSI currently has no partial-gravity data, but microgravity and normal-gravity results can help establish bounds for intermediate conditions. APULA uses these two gravity environments as reference points to explore what may happen in between.

Who It Is For and What It Gives Them

The brief identifies professors, students, aerospace researchers, and aerospace engineers as its intended audience. APULA was designed around one central question:

"I have a habitat atmosphere. Which investigations are relevant to it, and what does the available evidence tell me about how a fire might behave?"

What APULA offers

  • Finds relevant research. Identifies investigations that match a selected fire-safety scenario, without requiring users to browse the repository manually.
  • Enables comparison. Shows how investigations differ in their experimental conditions and the variables they tested.
  • Makes its reasoning transparent. Connects every ranking and prediction to its underlying equations or supporting experimental runs.
  • Makes complex relationships easier to understand. Uses the 3D flame chamber and phase charts to illustrate how oxygen concentration, pressure, and gravity influence combustion, including the Moon-habitat scenario highlighted in the brief (30% O₂ or more at 10.2 psi or less).

Intended impact. To bridge the gap between extensive combustion research and its practical implications for crewed environments, while highlighting areas where evidence remains limited, particularly partial gravity, to help guide future testing. Beyond space exploration, it also highlights the potential Earth applications of these investigations, from mist extinguishers and smoke detection to improved firefighter equipment.

How It Works

Physics Modelling

The engine is a set of closed-form relations, chosen so every output can be traced to an equation a reviewer can read.

1. Convective Velocity and Electrohydrodynamic Scaling

1.1 Froude Buoyant Draft Velocity

(1)

v_b = 22 · √max(0, g)

Upward natural-convection draft (cm/s) from thermal buoyancy at any gravity level g between 0 and 1, anchored to a 22 cm/s Earth (1 g) baseline.

1.2 ACME E-FIELD Electrohydrodynamic Ion-Wind Velocity

(2)

v_ion = 0.008 · E

Vertical ion-drag drift (cm/s) when an external electric field E (V/cm) pushes chemi-ionized flame cations in microgravity.

1.3 Pythagorean Mixed-Convection Effective Velocity

(3)

v_eff = √( v_fan² + (v_b + v_ion)² )

Combines horizontal forced fan flow with the vertical buoyant and ion-wind draft at right angles, giving the total oxidizer supply velocity without dividing by zero at 0 g.

1.4 Electrohydrodynamic Equivalent Gravity

(4)

g_eq = ( (v_b + v_ion) / 22 )²

Translates the combined vertical draft back into an apparent partial-gravity level. At E = 1100 V/cm in 0 g, the model reproduces Lunar (0.16 g) buoyancy.

2. Dual-Limit Flammability and Pressure Scaling

2.1 Stagnant Diffusive/Radiative Quenching Penalty (Low-Flow Branch)

(5)

ΔLOI_low = 4.8 · ((2 − v_eff) / 2)^1.25 if v_eff < 2 cm/s
ΔLOI_low = 0 if v_eff ≥ 2 cm/s

Raises the required oxygen threshold when airflow drops below 2 cm/s because stagnant microgravity flames suffocate in their own CO₂ product shell and lose heat via radiation.

2.2 Olson/T’ien Dual-Limit Flammability & Damköhler Scaling

(6)

ΔLOI_high = 0.04 · (v_eff − 12)^1.4 if v_eff > 12 cm/s
ΔLOI_high = 0 if v_eff ≤ 12 cm/s

Increases the minimum oxygen requirement above 12 cm/s as high convective airflow strips heat faster than the chemical reaction zone can replenish it.

2.3 Sub-Atmospheric Damköhler Pressure Scaling Factor

(7)

S_P = (P / 14.7)^−0.25

Scales the flammability boundary for reduced spacecraft cabin pressures P (psi) to account for lower bimolecular gas-phase collision rates relative to standard sea-level pressure (14.7 psi).

2.4 Composite Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI)

(8)

LOI = clamp( [ LOI_base + 0.22 · log2(τ / 0.35) + ΔLOI_low + ΔLOI_high + 0.32 · CO2% ] · (P / 14.7)^−0.25 , 8, 99 )

Determines the minimum oxygen percentage required to sustain combustion by combining baseline material flammability (LOI_base), sample thickness (τ in mm), ventilation penalties, CO₂ dilution, and cabin pressure scaling.

2.5 Ignition Margin

(9)

ΔO2 = O2% − LOI

Measures how far the ambient cabin oxygen concentration sits above (sustained burn, ∆O₂ >0) or below (extinction, ∆O₂ ≤ 0) the calculated Limiting Oxygen Index.

3. Flame Spread Rate, Thermal Kinetics & 3D Plume Morphology

3.1 Solid-Fuel Opposed/Concurrent Flame Spread Rate

(10)

V_f = clamp( 0.18 · (O2% − LOI) · √max(0.35, v_eff) · k_spread / τ^0.65 , 0, 75 )

Predicts the surface flame propagation speed (mm/s) across solid fuels as a function of excess oxygen margin, square-root boundary-layer velocity, material volatility (k_spread), and thermal thickness (τ ).

3.2 Cool-Flame vs. Hot-Flame Adiabatic Temperature

(11)

if regime = COOL_FLAME_CFI_G

T_ad = clamp( 560 + 1.8 · O2% , 550, 750 )

otherwise
T_ad = clamp( 1350 + 28 · ΔO2 + 3.2 · v_eff − 14 · CO2% , 1200, 2400 )

Separates low-temperature alkylperoxy cool flames (550–750 K) from standard hot diffusion flames (1200–2400 K) based on the active combustion regime and oxygen margin.

3.3 3D Flame Aspect Ratio (Spherical-to-Teardrop Elongation)

(12)

AR = L / W = clamp( 1.0 + v_eff / 7.0 + 1.7 · g , 1.0, 9.0 )

Controls the length-to-width stretching of the 3D WebGL flame mesh from a pure sphere (AR = 1.0) in stagnant microgravity to an elongated teardrop (AR > 1.0) under forced flow or

gravity.

3.4 Cross-Flow Plume Tilt Angle

(13)

θ_tilt = atan2( v_b + v_ion , max(0.5, v_fan) ) · 180 / π

Computes the exact inclination angle (in degrees) of the 3D flame plume by taking the inverse tangent of vertical buoyant/ion draft over horizontal fan velocity.

3.5 Partial-Gravity Froude Bounding Envelope (0.16g Moon & 0.38g Mars)

(14)

LOI(g, P) = LOI_0g(P) + √g · ( LOI_1g(P) − LOI_0g(P) )

Interpolates Lunar (g = 0.16) and Martian (g = 0.38) flammability boundaries strictly between empirical 0g ventilated flight data and 1g Earth upward flammability baselines.

Dashboard Walkthrough

Executive Mission Banner: How This SI System Works

The banner frames the problem before the user touches a control, using three cards.

Card 1: Why NASA PSI Data Matters. The data maps onto three fire-safety pillars:

  • Prevention (BASS / SAFFIRE-3). Screens spacecraft polymers and textiles in microgravity flow ducts and in the large-scale Saffire experiments flown on Cygnus, so habitat cabins can avoid easily ignited materials.
  • Detection (SAME / DAFT). Compares sub-micron smoke particles with 1–20 µm cabin and lunar dust, the distinction a detector needs to avoid nuisance alarms. During Artemis II, the crew reported a smoke detector alarm with Orion about 80,000 miles from Earth. We use it only to show why detection matters on crewed missions.
  • Suppression (FLEX / FLEX-2). Quantifies CO₂, helium and fine-water-mist extinguishment of burning liquid-fuel droplets in microgravity, informing suppression design for crewed habitats.

Card 2: Theory vs. Empirical Proof. Contrasts what the model computes with what NASA measured.

Card 3: Live Dataset Status Badge. Shows the active source, datum/masterPsiData.ts (a pre-loaded 8-campaign masterfile), so users always know which data is behind what they see.

Habitat Presets & 7 Physics Sliders

Six one-click habitat presets set the scenario: ISS, Lunar Base, Mars Habitat, EVA Suit, Earth, and ACME CFI-G. Seven controls then refine it:

  • oxygen concentration
  • cabin pressure
  • airflow
  • gravity
  • electric field
  • fuel material (six options, from thin PMMA film to heptane droplet)
  • CO₂ dilution

Every other section updates from these inputs.

Live Physics Readout & SVG Flame Plume / Inside-Out Burner Wireframe

The readout reports the flame regime, limiting oxygen index, ignition margin, spread rate, flame temperature, effective velocity and equivalent gravity. Next to it, a 2D wireframe draws the flame plume and the inside-out burner from the computed flame length and width, with a flicker frequency estimated from the same numbers.

Interactive 3D Microgravity Wind-Tunnel & Flame Morphology Chamber

A three.js chamber renders the flame in 3D. As gravity, flow and electric field change, it morphs from a pale blue diffusion sphere at 0 g into a tilted, buoyant teardrop. It is driven by the same numbers as the readout, so what you see is what the model computes.

Phase-Space Flammability Matrices: Partial-Gravity Bounding Envelope & Microgravity Ventilation U-Curve

Two views of the same boundary:

  • Partial-gravity bounding envelope. The 0 g (ventilated) and 1 g (Earth) limiting-oxygen curves with the Moon (0.16 g) and Mars (0.38 g) region between them, zoomed to the 12–38% O₂ range so the curves stay readable, with empirical flight points pinned on top.
  • Microgravity ventilation U-curve. Limiting oxygen against airflow. It is high when the air is nearly still (stagnant flames smother) and when flow is strong (blow-off), and lowest at moderate flow. This is the dual-limit behavior the low-flow and high-flow penalties encode.

Dynamic PSI Investigation Ranker with Data Provenance Badges

All 13 investigations receive a relevance score from 0–100 based on the selected scenario, with the reasoning behind each score displayed alongside it. Users can further narrow the results using two filters:

  • Pillar: All, Prevention, Detection, or Suppression
  • Provenance: All, Empirical CSV Loaded, Physics Simulated, or Future Lunar Flight

Each investigation card displays a live row count, clearly distinguishing studies with loaded experimental data from those only included in the catalog.

Intra- vs. Inter-Investigation Comparison Matrix

Select any two investigations to compare their experimental setups, including which variables were held constant and which were varied within and across studies. This answers the brief's question about how tests from the same investigation differed, and how different investigations compare.

Empirical NASA Flight Test Matcher

For the current scenario, the matcher returns the five closest real flight runs by weighted distance over oxygen, pressure, airflow and gravity. It keeps the model honest: a prediction far from every real run is visibly an extrapolation.

Tools and Technology

  • Framework: Next.js 15 (App Router), React 19
  • Language: TypeScript
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS 3
  • 3D: three.js, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei
  • Charts and flame field: SVG generated by the physics engine
  • Data: 654 flight rows bundled from the PSI-derived master file, parsed at load, no backend
  • Hardware: none; runs in the browser

Everything is client-side and bundled, so the app has no server dependency and can be demoed offline.

Considerations

  • Combustion Physics Engine. The deterministic semi-empirical combustion solver, covering Biot curvature scaling, 0g to 1g stability bounds, and L1 flight-run matching, is isolated inside combustionPhysicsEngine.ts alongside the pre-loaded 654-run NASA PSI dataset in masterPsiData.ts so parameter sweeps compute locally in real time without server latency and remain regression-tested by verifyPhysics.ts.
  • Visualization and Scientific Transparency. To keep outputs transparent rather than opaque, ThreeFlameChamber.tsx and FlammabilityPhaseCharts.tsx map computed regimes onto a 60 FPS WebGL flame chamber and clustered empirical U-curves, while metricAnnotations.ts and MetricAnnotationPopover.tsx surface live equation X-rays alongside MEASURED, ESTIMATED, INFERRED, and DEFAULTED provenance badges.
  • Dashboard Architecture and Interface. The single-page layout in page.tsx and the design tokens in globals.css synchronize environment controls, live telemetry cards, phase matrices, and NASA campaign tables within one interface so spacecraft flammability limits and spaceflight evidence can be evaluated side by side.

What Makes It Creative?

  • Electric field as a gravity dial. Turning the ACME E-FIELD result into a slider that moves a flame from 0 g toward Lunar buoyancy, and showing the equivalent gravity, makes an obscure experiment tangible.
  • The envelope view. Instead of pretending to know Moon and Mars flammability, the charts show what 0 g and 1 g data permit, which is the honest framing of the brief's own claim.
  • Interpretation, not just search. The tool does not stop at listing investigations; it ties them to a scenario, a regime and a set of real runs.
  • Physics you can see. A flame that morphs from a blue sphere to a tilted teardrop as gravity and flow change, driven by the same numbers as the readout.
  • History as context. A separate layer of reference events (Apollo 1, the 1997 Mir oxygen-candle fire, Saffire flight tests) sits beside the PSI data and is clearly labeled, with unknowns left blank instead of filled in.
